result: In 76 CCC ME/CFS vs 73 controls, flow cytometry showed lower Tregs, higher NKT-like cells, lower NKG2C+ and higher CD69+ and CD56bright NK cells; an NKG2C+Treg model classified 70% correctly.
reason: Measures NK and T-cell phenotypes, not NK cytotoxicity; no atlas finding covers NK subsets or Tregs.

result: In 76 CCC ME/CFS vs 73 controls, flow cytometry showed lower Tregs, higher NKT-like cells, lower NKG2C+ and higher CD69+ and CD56bright NK cells; an NKG2C+Treg model classified 70% correctly.
reason: NKT-like (CD3+CD56+) cells are not MAIT cells and CD8 memory subsets were not reported; no matching finding.

result: In 85 CFS vs 29 controls doing 30-70% MVC grip with feedback on fMRI, patients showed a bias toward less effort at 70% with reduced DLPFC feedback activity, higher SMA activity and reduced SMA-sensorimotor connectivity, scaling with state fatigue and beliefs.
reason: Grip-force fMRI of motor-network activity matches the motor fatigability finding; it does not use the EEfRT the effort-preference finding is about, so that is a secondary fit only.

result: In 24 ME/CFS vs 24 matched sedentary controls, cardiac structure and exercise capacity on CPET were similar; cytokines 18 h after exercise discriminated groups (kappa 0.62).
reason: Reports no difference in exercise capacity vs sedentary controls, a null result, not an extension; small sample and the test may have been submaximal.

result: 51-plex Luminex cytokines 18 h after exercise discriminated 24 ME/CFS from 24 sedentary controls better than baseline (sPLS-DA kappa 0.62; CD40L, PAI, IL-1beta, IFN-alpha, CXCL1).
reason: Circulating proteins in the recovery phase separating patients from sedentary controls is the same concept on a smaller panel; small and no direction or multiplicity detail.

result: In 20 CFS vs 20 sedentary controls, HRV by finger plethysmography showed no group or interaction effects during physical and emotional stress (P 0.18-0.75).
reason: Same measure (HRV) with a null group effect; small sample and plethysmography-based HRV.

result: In 20 CFS vs 20 sedentary controls, transcranial Doppler CBF showed no group or interaction effects during mild cycling or emotional stress.
reason: No tilt or orthostatic challenge was used, so it does not test the tilt finding; resting-CBF finding uses ASL/SPECT perfusion, not Doppler during exercise.

result: Plasma BNP was higher in 42 Fukuda CFS than 10 controls (P=0.013), and patients with high BNP (>400 pg/mL) had smaller end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes on cardiac MRI, unrelated to disease duration.
reason: Builds on the earlier cardiac MRI finding by linking reduced volumes to a BNP subgroup within patients; it is not an independent patient-vs-control volume replication.

result: In 80 female CFS vs 91 female controls, NR3C1-1F glucocorticoid receptor promoter was slightly hypomethylated at several CpGs, with only CpG_8 surviving correction (1.3% vs 1.5%).
reason: No challenge test; it offers a candidate mechanism (enhanced GR sensitivity) for the enhanced-feedback finding, so extends, not replicates; tiny absolute differences.

result: CSF miRNAs did not differ at rest between GWI (22), CFS (43) and controls (22); after submaximal exercise CFS showed 12 diminished CSF miRNAs, a pattern distinct from GWI phenotypes.
reason: Neuro/omics domain: post-exercise CSF microRNA changes are not covered by any atlas finding; small groups and many comparisons.
